key_insight: A lightweight, application-targeted transformer inpainting module can reliably complete missing textures in real-time 3D streams from sparse multi‑camera rigs, producing coherent surfaces and far fewer visual artifacts than simple heuristic fill-ins.
problem_solved: Addresses holes and incomplete surfaces in rendered views caused by limited camera coverage in real‑time multi‑camera 3D streaming, where existing heuristic hole‑filling produces inconsistencies and visual artifacts.
method: Learned transformer-based inpainting operating on projected texture/view patches to predict plausible content for missing regions.
Geometry- and view-aware conditioning (camera poses, depth/confidence maps, and neighbouring views) to ensure cross-view consistency.
Latency‑aware design for streaming: efficient attention (patch/windowed processing), temporal-consistency losses, and lightweight model optimizations for real‑time deployment.
impact: Enables higher-fidelity AR/VR experiences with fewer cameras and lower bandwidth/hardware costs by replacing brittle heuristics with learned, consistent texture completion; provides a template for deploying transformer models under strict latency constraints.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse camera inputs → geometry/depth projection → transformer inpainting → final rendered frame (with latency annotation).
Before/after comparison: rendered views with heuristic filling vs. transformer inpainting to highlight artifact reduction.
Attention/patch visualization: heatmap showing where the transformer borrows context from other views/regions.
Latency vs. quality chart: tradeoff curve showing real‑time capable settings and visual fidelity improvements.
paper_title: Transformer-Based Inpainting for Real-Time 3D Streaming in Sparse Multi-Camera Setups
paper_authors: Leif Van Holland, Domenic Zingsheim, Mana Takhsha, Hannah Dröge, Patrick Stotko
